name: Wabash Ways Atlas - trails & waterways (PLSS draft)

metadata.note: Geometry APPROXIMATE - points at PLSS section centers (2nd PM, ~0.5mi), trails/rivers as waypoint polylines. Replace with meander-table geometry for final. Protocol: Nation review on reserve/village/trace features before publish.

properties.name: Wabash River
properties.description: The main stem; surveyed meander banks across the county. Approx course from PLSS crossings (NE Carroll Co. -> SW past Lafayette toward Attica).
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes (meander tables)

properties.name: Tippecanoe River
properties.description: Chief northern tributary; meanders S/SW to join the Wabash at the mouth in T24N-R3W Sec 8 (the confluence by Prophetstown). Islands incl. a cluster in T26N-R3W Sec 3.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Pine Creek (Big Pine Creek)
properties.description: Major western drainage, SE course; whetstone-grit falls & mill seats in T21N-R7W. Flows toward the Wabash near Attica.
properties.source: PLSS notes (named 'Pine Creek'/'Big Pine Creek'/'Pine River')

properties.name: Wild Cat Creek
properties.description: Crosses the Wea Plain NW/W toward the Wabash. Named in PLSS notes; the Prophet's refuge after the 1811 battle.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Burnett's Creek
properties.description: Willow-lined stream on the W/NW edge of the Tippecanoe battlefield; Harrison's army camped on the oak rise above it the night of Nov 6-7, 1811 (rear line guarded the creek). Flows SW past Battle Ground to the Wabash. Named for the Burnett family -- almost certainly the metis Potawatomi Burnetts (cf. Burnet's Reserve RS-01, same township); eponym not stated in battle histories (VERIFY). Cross-ref F-001/016/152/155.
properties.source: DeHart/battle accounts; PLSS

properties.name: Harrison Creek
properties.description: Small creek beginning near Battle Ground, flowing east; named for Gen. W.H. Harrison.
properties.source: standard

properties.name: Wea Creek (Weeawe)
properties.description: Miami-named creek entering the Wabash from the SE; the only cultural name in the Ouiatanon township notes.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Pouceaupichieux Creek
properties.description: French-derived creek name; enters the Wabash from the SW (spelling approximate).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Flint Creek
properties.description: Creek at whose mouth the 6-section Burnet reserve sat (T22N-R6W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Stony Creek
properties.description: Named on the T25N-R2W plat near Mary Wells' Reserve.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Little Pine Creek
properties.description: Named creek, SE course (T24N-R6W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Brosher Creek
properties.description: Named creek in T21N-R7W (spelling uncertain).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Great Wabash Trail
properties.description: Principal Native N-S route following the Wabash (Vincennes-Ouiatanon-Kekionga). PLSS confirms the river corridor WAS the route; plotted along the Wabash.
properties.source: Dunn/DeHart; PLSS

properties.name: Great Sauk Trail
properties.description: Detroit -> SW Michigan (now US-12/old Chicago Rd) -> near La Porte, Indiana -> around the head of Lake Michigan to Chicago, the wild-rice country of Green Bay, and the Lake Superior copper mines; a ~2,000-mi thoroughfare. Branch through Ontario to Niagara & Montreal. [Hinsdale 1931; Treaty of Chicago 1821 Art.6]
properties.source: standard

properties.name: Potawatomi Trail of Death (1838)
properties.description: 1838 forced-removal route: Twin Lakes(Plymouth)->Logansport->Battle Ground vicinity->Williamsport->Danville IL->Kansas. Cross-ref F-040.
properties.source: removal record

properties.name: Potawatomi-Miami Trail
properties.description: Fort Wayne-Chicago trade route (Maumee<->Lake Michigan via St. Joseph watershed/Elkhart Co.); distinct from the Sauk Trail. [Wilson 1919 p.431 corroborates: a 'road from Fort Wayne to Chicago' crossed the MI-IN line at the NW corner of Elkhart Co.]
properties.source: potawatomi-miamitrail.org; standard

properties.name: Lafayette-Chicago Road
properties.description: State wagon road labeled 'Lafayette'<->'Chicago' on the T26N-R7W plat; crossed on many section lines through the Grand Prairie (Benton Co.).
properties.source: PLSS plat/notes T26N-R7W

properties.name: Wabash-Rockville Wagon Road
properties.description: Wagon road 'supposed to lead from the Wabash to Rockville', NW course (T26N-R6W/R7W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Barnett's Road
properties.description: Named early road across the N of the Lafayette township toward Abraham Burnett's place/reserve.
properties.source: PLSS plat T23N-R4W (labeled)

properties.name: Wea Trail
properties.description: Wea Plain <-> Ouiatanon/Wabash crossing.
properties.source: Dunn/DeHart

properties.name: Wabash-Maumee Portage (Kekionga)
properties.description: The 'glorious gate' carrying-place between the Great Lakes (Maumee) and Wabash watersheds at Fort Wayne. Cross-ref F-049.
properties.source: Dunn Vol.I + Hulbert Vol.7 (Wabash-Maumee 'Petite Riviere' route)

properties.name: Indian trail (confluence)
properties.description: 'an Indian trail' logged in the Tippecanoe meander at the Wabash-Tippecanoe mouth.
properties.source: PLSS notes T24N-R3W

properties.name: Old Indian trail (deep hollow)
properties.description: 'old Indian trail N&S, a deep hollow' logged on the line btw Secs 25&36.
properties.source: PLSS notes T26N-R7W

properties.name: Burnet's Reserve (A. Burnett, Potawatomi)
properties.description: On the Wabash by the battlefield; NW boundary = the plat's N50E line.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Burnett Reserve (1,280 ac)
properties.description: SE of T25N-R3W, straddling into R2W.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Burnet 6-section Reserve (mouth of Flint Creek)
properties.description: Six sections at the mouth of Flint Creek.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: P. Langlois Reservation (1,250 ac)
properties.description: 'Ten oldest children' of the French-Potawatomi trader Langlois, on the Wabash near Lafayette.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Wyandot Reserve 'Long Hair & others' (5 sec)
properties.description: Wyandot reserve + village on the Wea Plain. Cross-ref F-153.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Jean B. Cicot Reserve (640 ac)
properties.description: Cicot/Cicotte family reserve on the Wabash. Cross-ref F-121.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Z. Cicot's Children Reserve (960 ac)
properties.description: On the Wabash (Carroll Co.). Cross-ref F-121.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Mary Chalilie/Challis Reserve (640 ac)
properties.description: SW of T22N-R7W, straddling T21N-R7W (name uncertain).
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Children of A. Bondie Reserve (2 sec)
properties.description: Opposite L'Isle a l'Aille.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Mary Wells' Reserve (640 ac)
properties.description: SW T25N-R2W near Stony Creek.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Connor's Reserve (J.W. & H. Connor, 1,920 ac)
properties.description: Long tract on the SW bank of the Wabash.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Kickapoo Village (Wabash)
properties.description: 'an Indian village occupied by Kickapoos' on the Wabash bottom.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Wyandot Village (Long Hair)
properties.description: Drawn village on the Wyandot reserve. Cross-ref F-153.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: French/Potawatomi 'Village des...'
properties.description: Village by the Langlois reserve on the Wabash.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Morris Trading House ('Morris' landing')
properties.description: 'a Trading house formerly used by a Mr. Morris'; drawn as a building on the plat.
properties.source: PLSS plats/notes

properties.name: Petrifying (tufa) Spring
properties.description: 'a remarkable Spring... elevated by a mass of petrified substance... 3.5 ft above the common level.'
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Sulphur/Iron Water
properties.description: 'water sulphury or of Iron cast' past a Pine Creek crossing.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Pine Creek Falls & Mill Seat
properties.description: 'considerable falls... rock bottom, whetstone grit & slate stone'; a mill seat.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Mill Seat (30-in fall)
properties.description: 'a good mill seat, fall of 30 in nearly perpendicular.'
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Muskrat Pond/Harbour
properties.description: Large pond/marsh complex; 'many Muskrat houses & Fish' (also T26N-R4W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Racoon Pond
properties.description: Named pond on the W line of T26N-R5W.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Fish Pond
properties.description: Named pond by Muskrat Pond (T26N-R4W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Rush Pond
properties.description: Named recurring wet pond, N-central T26N-R7W.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Grand Prairie (label)
properties.description: The great upper-Wabash prairie (also T25N-R4W, T26N-R7W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Pretty Prairie (label)
properties.description: 'enter Pretty Prairie (so called)'.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Anderson's Grove
properties.description: Named timber grove (also T25N-R6W).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Walnut Grove
properties.description: 'This is called the Walnut grove'; a house nearby.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Finch's Grove
properties.description: 'known as Finches Grove, from the most influential man in the grove.'
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: White Oak Grove
properties.description: 'what is called the W. Oak grove.'
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: L'Isle a l'Aille (Wabash island)
properties.description: Named island in the Wabash (T25N-R2W plat).
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Ridge dividing Wabash & Iroquois waters
properties.description: Low ridge (<25 ft) dividing the Wabash and Iroquois/Illinois drainages.
properties.source: PLSS notes

properties.name: Tippecanoe Battlefield
properties.description: The 1811 battleground (F-001/016/152).
properties.source: folklore master

properties.name: Ouiatanon site
properties.description: French post & Wea towns, S bank of the Wabash (F-054).
properties.source: folklore master

properties.name: Prophetstown / Wabash-Tippecanoe confluence
properties.description: Mouth of the Tippecanoe (F-001).
properties.source: folklore master

properties.name: Buffalo Trace (Vincennes Trace)
properties.description: The great E-W artery of southern Indiana: Falls of the Ohio (New Albany) -> Paoli -> Shoals -> Vincennes. Worn first by migrating bison, then the main Native and pioneer road to the lower Wabash. (Loads its Part-A locked ID into the atlas.)
properties.source: Wilson, Early Indiana Trails & Surveys (1919); Vincennes Trace

properties.name: Thorntown Trace
properties.description: Connector from the Wea towns/Ouiatanon SE to Thorntown (the Eel River Miami reserve, Boone Co.) and on toward central Indiana. Ties the Ouiatanon hub to the Thorntown band.
properties.source: Wilson 1919; Dunn glossary (F-123)

properties.name: Strawtown / Lafayette Trace (Tecumseh's route)
properties.description: Prehistoric game trail -> Native trace: Delaware capital at Anderson -> ford at Strawtown (White R.) -> NW to the Wildcat & Wea prairies on the Wabash. The route Tecumseh rode from Anderson to Prophetstown; plowed under by the 1880s. FOOTPRINT-CONNECTING.
properties.source: Wilson 1919; IN.gov history blog (Lafayette/Strawtown Trace)

properties.name: Mississinewa Trail
properties.description: Up the Mississinewa River from the Wabash at Peru through the Miami villages to the Mississinewa towns (site of the 1812 Mississinewa campaign); connects toward Lake Manitou.
properties.source: Wilson 1919; Dunn (cross-ref F-124/144)

properties.name: Strawtown-Kekionga Trail
properties.description: N-S trail crossing the Lafayette/Strawtown Trace at Strawtown and running to the Miami capital Kekionga (Fort Wayne).
properties.source: IN.gov history blog; Wilson 1919

properties.name: Ouiatanon-Chicago Trace
properties.description: Native trace NW from Ouiatanon across the Grand Prairie (Benton Co.) to the Kankakee and Chicago; the Indian precursor underlying the later Lafayette-Chicago wagon road (cross-ref TR-023).
properties.source: Wilson 1919

properties.name: St. Joseph-Kankakee Portage
properties.description: St. Joseph R. landing near South Bend, SW ~4-5 miles across the prairie to the Kankakee marsh (near the sec. 7/8 line); the continental divide carry used by Marquette, La Salle, and the French voyageurs. 'German's Portage' was a variant landing a mile or more shorter. [Baker, The St. Joseph-Kankakee Portage, 1899]
properties.source: Wilson 1919 (Kankakee-St. Joseph route); Hulbert Vol.7; Baker 1899

properties.name: Red Banks Trail
properties.description: Henderson KY ('Red Banks') -> Evansville -> Princeton -> Vincennes; near-due N-S, ~1 mi W of the R10/R11 line. Harmar's 1787 route.

properties.name: Yellow Banks Trail
properties.description: Rockport (Ohio R.) N through Spencer/Warrick/Pike to the Delaware summer camp at the forks of White R.; via Chrisney, Gentryville, Dale, Otwell; crossed the Patoka at a ford near Jasper. Delaware 'Weesoe Wusapinuk'.

properties.name: Rome Trace
properties.description: Rome (Perry Co., orig. 'Washington') NW via Fulda, Mariah Hill, N of Dale to the SW corner of Dubois Co.; lost at the Freeman line ~2 mi NE of Pleasantville; joined the Yellow Banks Trail near the Pike Co. line.

properties.name: Shawnee Trace
properties.description: Southern Illinois -> Vincennes; two traces joined near the 'beauty spots' ~6 mi NW of Mt. Carmel IL. 'Shawnee' = 'Southerner'. Only incidentally in Indiana.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.360,455

properties.name: Salt Route (Salt Trace)
properties.description: Vincennes -> White R. crossing near Hazleton -> Patoka at John Severns' (3 mi N of Princeton) -> SW to the Wabash near the mouth of the Little Wabash -> the Illinois salt works (Saline Creek, nr Shawneetown). Crossed the Wabash 'just below New Harmony'.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.396-397

properties.name: Kibbey's Road
properties.description: First road across the whole state: Cincinnati -> Vincennes (cut by Capt. E. Kibbey, 1799). Via Milan/Dearborn Co., Madison, New Lexington, Salem, French Lick, the forks of White R. ~201 mi. Became the north fork of the Buffalo trace.

properties.name: Vallonia Trace
properties.description: Vallonia (old fort, Jackson Co.) SE through Washington & Scott Cos. into Clark's Grant near the Pigeon Roost, to old Springville (nr Charlestown) and the Falls of the Ohio; crossed the Muscatatuck. The 'Aaron Burr cabin' stood on it.

properties.name: Whetzel's Trace
properties.description: Jacob Whetzel's 1818 trace through the New Purchase: Laurel (Whitewater R., Franklin Co.) W ~60 mi to the West Fork of White R. at Waverly; ~7 mi below Rushville, 4 mi above Shelbyville, N of Boggstown. Permission from Delaware Chief Anderson.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.399-401

properties.name: Blue River Trace
properties.description: Ohio R. at Fredonia (mouth of Blue R.) N via Hardinsburg to the Buffalo trace near Samuel Hay's cabin on the W bank of Little Blue R. (~34.25 mi from Clark's Grant). Emigrant entry route after 1807.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.381-384

properties.name: Buck Creek Trace
properties.description: Harrison Co. (R4E): Ohio R. -> Corydon -> the Buffalo trace; crossed the S fork of Buck creek twice. Squire Boone's mill and 'cave-sepulchre' nearby.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 p.357

properties.name: Illinois Trace
properties.description: The 'Old Buffalo trace' running W from Vincennes into Illinois (from Clark's Grant); the W line of the Vincennes tract crossed it. Clark's 1779 approach route is linked to it.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.361,420

properties.name: Michigan Road
properties.description: 1828-30 state road, 100 ft wide: Michigan City (Trail Creek/Lake Michigan) -> South Bend -> Rochester -> Logansport (Eel R.) -> Indianapolis -> Madison. Touches the footprint corridor at Logansport.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 pp.439-441

properties.name: Vincennes-Fort Harrison Trail
properties.description: Indian trail N from Vincennes, crossing the Freeman line near Carlisle, past Terre Haute to Fort Harrison (on the Wabash).
properties.source: Wilson 1919 p.361

properties.name: Fort Wayne-Nottawasepe Trail
properties.description: Indian trail from Fort Wayne NW to Nottawasepe (Michigan); crossed the state line ~6 mi W of the NE corner of LaGrange Co.
properties.source: Wilson 1919 p.432 (MI-IN line survey)

properties.name: Coldwater-Fort Wayne Trail
properties.description: Indian trail between Coldwater (Michigan) and Fort Wayne; crossed the state line just N of Fremont, IN (near James Lake).
properties.source: Wilson 1919 p.432 (MI-IN line survey)

properties.name: Chicago Portage
properties.description: The continental hinge Chicago R. (Lake Michigan) <-> Des Plaines/Illinois R. (Mississippi). Marquette wintered on it 1674-75; named in the 1795 Treaty of Greenville. The reason Chicago exists.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Fox-Wisconsin Portage ('The Grand Portage')
properties.description: Fox R. (Green Bay/Great Lakes) <-> Wisconsin R. (Mississippi) at present Portage, WI. Crossed by Nicollet (1634) and Joliet & Marquette (1673); guarded by Fort Winnebago.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Niagara Portage (Lake Erie <-> Lake Ontario)
properties.description: The carry around Niagara Falls between Lakes Ontario and Erie -- the great choke-point of the lower Lakes; long controlled by the Seneca and then contested by France and Britain.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Cuyahoga-Tuscarawas Portage ('the Portage Path')
properties.description: Lake Erie (Cuyahoga R.) <-> Ohio R. (Tuscarawas/Muskingum) at present Akron, OH; the 'Portage Path' was a surveyed treaty landmark (1785 Fort McIntosh line).
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Scioto-Sandusky Portage
properties.description: Lake Erie (Sandusky R.) <-> Ohio R. (Scioto) -- the central Ohio carry linking the Lakes to the Ohio down the Scioto.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Miami-St. Mary's (Loramie) Portage
properties.description: Great Miami R. (Ohio R. system) <-> St. Mary's R. (Maumee/Lake Erie) at Loramie's store; the SW Ohio carry between the Ohio and the Lakes.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Chautauqua Portage
properties.description: Lake Erie <-> Chautauqua Lake -> Allegheny/Ohio (Mississippi system); the shortest Lakes-to-Ohio carry, used by the French 1753 to reach the Allegheny.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Presque Isle-French Creek Portage
properties.description: Lake Erie (Presque Isle) <-> Riviere aux Boeufs (French Creek) -> Allegheny; the French 1753 fort chain (Presque Isle -> Le Boeuf) carry.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways of America, Vol.7 'Portage Paths' (1903), Gutenberg #41179

properties.name: Great Trail (tidewater -> Detroit)
properties.description: The principal E-W trunk: forks of the Ohio (Pittsburgh) -> Fort Laurens (Tuscarawas ford) -> Mohican John's Town -> Sandusky Bay -> Maumee Rapids (Perrysburg) -> Toledo -> Monroe -> Flat Rock -> Brownstown -> Detroit; N of Detroit it becomes the Saginaw & Mackinaw Trail. A Maumee branch entered Michigan at Morenci and joined the Chicago Trail at Allen.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails' | also in Hulbert Vol.2 Indian Thoroughfares (Ft Pitt->Big Beaver->Bolivar->Mohican John's Town->Sandusky->Detroit; Heckewelder 1796 map)

properties.name: Lake Erie Shore Trail
properties.description: South shore of Lake Erie: Toledo (where the Michigan trails converged) -> Sandusky Bay -> Cleveland -> Erie PA -> Buffalo/Niagara NY; closely followed by the modern lakeshore highway. Extends east as the Mohawk Trail to the Hudson.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails' | also Hulbert Vol.2 (Niagara->Presque Isle->Sandusky->Detroit, 'second beach'; Heckewelder 1796)

properties.name: Scioto Trail
properties.description: Branched from the Great/Shore trails at Sandusky Bay, up the Sandusky R. to the portage, down the Scioto to the Ohio, then across Kentucky (Warriors' Path) to Cumberland Gap and the South. The copper-and-shell trade artery: Michigan copper south, marine shell north.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails' | also Hulbert Vol.2 (Sandusky valley->Scioto->Ohio; Kanawha branch to Pt Pleasant; Filson/Hutchins maps)

properties.name: Montreal Trail (Detroit -> Prophetstown/Ouiatenon)
properties.description: THE Great Lakes land-link into the footprint: an old trail from Montreal following the Chicago Trail from Detroit, branching at Fort St. Joseph (Niles) and leading SOUTH to the Tippecanoe River, Prophet's Town, and Ouiatenon on the Wabash. From Ouiatenon, water route to New Orleans (Eddy: 1,871 mi). FOOTPRINT-CONNECTING.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails' (Eddy 1816 & Hutchins 1778 maps)

properties.name: Mahoning Trail
properties.description: The most direct Detroit <-> forks-of-the-Ohio route: up the north bend of the Mahoning R. (E Ohio), then W to join the Great Trail near Sandusky Bay.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails' | also Hulbert Vol.2 (runners' bypass Ft Pitt->Beaver/Mahoning->Cuyahoga-Tuscarawas portage->Sandusky)

properties.name: Saginaw & Mackinaw Trail
properties.description: Detroit -> Pontiac -> Flint -> Saginaw R. -> up the Tittabawassee to Edenville, where it forked for the Grand Traverse region and for Cheboygan/the Straits of Mackinac. Followed by the Dixie Highway from Toledo through Detroit, Pontiac, Flint.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails'

properties.name: Grand River Trail
properties.description: Detroit -> Grand Rapids (mouth of the Grand), through Oakland, Livingston, Ingham, Ionia, Kent counties; followed the Cedar R. much of the way. Leaves Detroit as Grand River Avenue / the Grand River Road; a trail network fanned out at the Grand Rapids.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails'

properties.name: Territorial Trail
properties.description: Crossed the Chicago/Sauk Trail at Ypsilanti, through Ann Arbor, the centers of Jackson & Calhoun counties, branching to Kalamazoo (uniting with the Chicago Trail in SE Berrien Co.) and to the mouths of the St. Joseph (St. Joseph) and Kalamazoo (Saugatuck).
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails'

properties.name: Potawatomi Trail (Huron River, Michigan)
properties.description: Followed the Huron R. from its mouth (Lake Erie) up to Portage Lake (Washtenaw/Livingston line), crossing the Chicago/Sauk Trail at Ypsilanti and passing Ann Arbor. Distinct from the Fort Wayne-Chicago Potawatomi-Miami Trail (TR-022).
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails'

properties.name: Mackinaw-St. Joseph Shore Trail
properties.description: Down the east shore of Lake Michigan: Mackinaw -> the Traverse bays -> Manistee/Mason/Oceana shore -> South Haven -> mouth of the St. Joseph (St. Joseph); below St. Joseph it touched the shore villages and JOINED THE SAUK TRAIL IN INDIANA, connecting for Chicago. FOOTPRINT-CONNECTING.
properties.source: Hinsdale, Archaeological Atlas of Michigan (1931), ch. 'Trails'

properties.name: Harmar's Road (1790)
properties.description: Harmar's 1790 campaign march, Fort Washington (Cincinnati) NW to the Maumee towns at Kekionga (Fort Wayne): via Lebanon, Fish-pot Ford (Little Miami), old Chillicothe, Mad R. near New Carlisle, Troy, Piqua (Great Miami), Loramie's Creek, St. Marys. Followed Clark's 1782 trace out of Cincinnati; Hardin's ambush fell on the Kickapoo path near the Eel R. ~11 mi from Fort Wayne.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.8 'Military Roads of the Mississippi Basin: The Conquest of the Old Northwest' (1904), Gutenberg #41167

properties.name: Wayne's Trace & the fort chain (1791-94)
properties.description: The military road and fort chain of the Old Northwest conquest: Fort Washington -> Ft. Hamilton -> Ft. St. Clair (Eaton) -> Ft. Jefferson -> Ft. Greene Ville -> Ft. Recovery (St. Clair's 1791 defeat) -> Ft. Adams -> Ft. Defiance (Auglaize-Maumee) -> down the Maumee to Fallen Timbers & Ft. Meigs (the Rapids). Wayne built Fort Wayne at Kekionga, 1794.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.8 'Military Roads of the Mississippi Basin: The Conquest of the Old Northwest' (1904), Gutenberg #41167 + standard campaign histories

properties.name: Hull's Road (1812)
properties.description: Hull's 1812 march to Detroit, the chief supply road of the NW theatre: Dayton/Urbana -> Ft. McArthur (Kenton) -> Ft. Findlay -> Ft. Meigs (Maumee Rapids) -> Brownstown -> Detroit.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.8 'Military Roads of the Mississippi Basin: The Conquest of the Old Northwest' (1904), Gutenberg #41167 + War-of-1812 histories

properties.name: Cuyahoga-Muskingum Trail (Old Muskingum Trail)
properties.description: Lake Erie <-> Ohio R. through the Delaware country: mouth of the Cuyahoga (Cleveland) -> the great portage to the Tuscarawas (Akron) -> down the Tuscarawas past the Crossing-place of the Muskingum (Bolivar) to the Delaware capital Gosh-goshing (Coshocton) -> down the Muskingum to Marietta.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Miami Trail
properties.description: War-and-trade path: the Great/Little Miami valleys converging to cross the Ohio near the mouth of the Miami (North Bend/Cincinnati), then through the Licking and Kentucky valleys to the Cumberland watershed; a branch joins the Warriors' Path through Cumberland Gap into Cherokee country.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Maumee / 'Miami-of-the-Lake' Trail
properties.description: Scioto -> Maumee connector: from Lower Shawnees Town (mouth of the Scioto) NW on the watershed between the Scioto and the two Miamis to the Maumee valley and the Miami town at Kekionga (Fort Wayne) -- the road on toward the Lake Michigan and Superior country.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902) (Hutchins map 1764)

properties.name: Venango Path
properties.description: The main landward Fort Pitt -> Lake Erie route and French-fort line: Fort Pitt N on the Allegheny/Beaver watershed to Fort Venango (Franklin), up French Creek (Riviere aux Boeufs) to Fort Le Boeuf (Waterford) and the portage to Fort Presque Isle (Erie).
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Scioto-Beaver Trail
properties.description: Second in Western importance to the Great Trail: Lower Shawnees Town up the Scioto/Tuscarawas to the Delaware country near Coshocton, then the Tuscarawas-Ohio watershed to 'Painted Post' and the Pennsylvania frontier at the Beaver. Traversed by Christopher Gist for the Ohio Company.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Scioto-Monongahela Trail
properties.description: Scioto country <-> the 'Long House' via the lower Ohio: Lower Shawnees Town E across Fairfield/Perry Cos. to Wallace Ridge and 'Big Rock', S to the Ohio opposite the mouth of the Little Kanawha (Belpre), crossing at Parkersburg, by Dry Ridge to the Monongahela. Tecumseh's party marched part of it.
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Iroquois Trail (Great Central Trail)
properties.description: The spine of the Six Nations' Long House and one of the longest independent thoroughfares on the continent: Hudson R. below Albany -> up the Mohawk valley -> Ft Stanwix (Rome) -> Oneida -> Onondaga (Syracuse, the council fire) -> Cayuga (Auburn) -> N of the Finger Lakes -> Seneca country (Canandaigua, Batavia) -> Niagara R. just S of the falls. Became the Genesee Rd / NY Central corridor. [NORTHEAST / Laurie's NY]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902) (Guy Johnson map 1771)

properties.name: Old Connecticut Path
properties.description: Boston/Cambridge -> Marlborough -> Grafton -> Oxford -> Springfield -> Albany; the Bay colonists' road to the Hudson, ~ the Boston & Albany RR alignment. [NORTHEAST]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: New Connecticut Path
properties.description: Parallel to the Old Connecticut Path: Cambridge -> Worcester -> Albany. [NORTHEAST]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Kittanning Path
properties.description: A preeminent traders' route over the Alleghenies: Kittanning on the Allegheny -> Kittanning Gorge/Point (nr Hollidaysburg) -> up the Juniata (Water Street, Alexandria) -> across the ridges -> Susquehanna/Carlisle -> Philadelphia. Became Forbes's Road (1758). [NORTHEAST/Appalachian]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Nemacolin's Path
properties.description: The 'bloody thoroughfare' VA/MD traffic converged on: Wills Creek (Ft Cumberland) -> Little Crossings -> Great Meadows -> Gist's Plantation (Mt Braddock) -> Stewart's Crossing (Connellsville) -> the forks of the Ohio (Pittsburgh). Became Washington's Rd, Braddock's Rd, the Cumberland/National Rd. [NORTHEAST/Appalachian]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Virginia Warriors' Path
properties.description: The great N-S war trail in the trough between the Blue Ridge and Cumberland ranges: Shenandoah/New R. valley -> Cumberland Gap -> Crab Orchard -> Danville -> the Falls of the Ohio (Louisville), on toward the Mississippi. Became Boone's Wilderness Road. [NORTHEAST/Appalachian->South]
properties.source: Hulbert, Historic Highways Vol.2 'Indian Thoroughfares' (1902)

properties.name: Allegheny Path
properties.description: Philadelphia->the Allegheny; the main E-W trader path (Armstrong Path a branch) [Wallace #001, p.19] | Philadelphia->Robin Hood's Ford->Paoli->Morgantown->Myerstown->Lebanon->Hershey->Hummelstown->Paxtang(Harrisburg); continues W as the Frankstown Path (PA-026). Oldest road in PA.

properties.name: Forbes Road (1758)
properties.description: The Raystown Path militarized by Gen. Forbes 1758: Harrisburg->Carlisle->Shippensburg->Ft Loudon(Cowan Gap)->Ft Littleton->Bedford->Ligonier->Bushy Run->Ft Pitt. Became the Pennsylvania Road (Appendix IV) [Wallace]
properties.source: Wallace, Indian Paths of Pennsylvania (1965)

properties.name: Washington's Path to Fort LeBoeuf (1753)
properties.description: Young George Washington's Dec 1753 mission: Logstown->Murthering Town(Harmony)->Portersville->West Liberty->the Venango Path->Venango(Franklin)->Cussewago(Meadville)->Little Cooley detour->Fort LeBoeuf(Waterford) (Appendix V) [Wallace]
properties.source: Wallace, Indian Paths of Pennsylvania (1965)

properties.name: Venango Path
properties.description: Pittsburgh(Shannopin's)->Evans City->Prospect->Harrisville->Barkeyville->Franklin(Venango)->up French Creek->Cambridge Springs->Fort Le Boeuf(Waterford)->Presque Isle(Erie); the chief Ft Pitt->Lake Erie military highway 1753-94 (cross-ref TR-059). [Wallace #117, p.170]
properties.source: Wallace, Indian Paths of Pennsylvania (1965)
